article.headline: Cheniere Energy Nears Record As LNG Exports Draw QatarEnergy Deals
article.deck: Cheniere sits 0.1% under the 300.99 buy point of a 29-week cup, with an early entry already live at 298.57.
body: Cheniere Energy turns natural gas into a liquid and ships it overseas. It owns and runs the Sabine Pass terminal in Cameron Parish, Louisiana, and the Corpus Christi terminal in Texas, along with the pipelines that feed them, including the 94-mile Creole Trail line into Sabine Pass. It trades in the energy group, which has 71% of its names above the 50-day line on the desk's list while the broader market sits in correction.

The stock rose 1.92, or 0.6%, to 300.59 on Monday on volume 1.27 times its 50-day average. It is up 54.6% year to date and 35.7% over the past year, and the close sits 0.6% below the 52-week high of 302.45.

The earnings show why. The June quarter showed earnings of $14.65 a share, up 100.7% from a year earlier, on revenue of $5.73 billion, up 23.5%. The record is lumpy: the March quarter showed a loss of $16.65 a share, after profits of $10.68 in December and $4.75 in September 2025. Revenue moved from $4.44 billion in September 2025 to $5.45 billion, $5.87 billion and $5.73 billion across the next three quarters.
The market values Cheniere at $62.08 billion. The stock trades at 22.75 times trailing earnings and 14.51 times forward estimates.

On the chart, Cheniere has built a 29-week cup that ran 25.7% deep from its March 30 high to its June 18 low. The buy point is 300.99 and the buy range runs to 316.04; Monday's close sits 0.1% below it. The stock has already closed above a downtrend line drawn from the March 30 high through the Sept. 1 high, at 298.57, an early entry while the base finishes. It sits 7.7% above its 50-day line at 279.07 and 18.3% above its 200-day line at 254.15, and 1.40 ATRs from the 21-day line at 283.49. RS rank is 85 of 99 on the desk's list; the RS line is 16.0% below its high.

Recent headlines said Cheniere signed deals with QatarEnergy and that U.S. LNG exporters are drawing fresh attention. Previews of the third-quarter report weighed the Qatar deals against global shocks.

The timing matters. Cheniere reports on Oct. 29, three sessions from now, with the stock sitting right at its buy point. A decisive close above 300.99 would complete the breakout; a reaction to the report could also set the next leg in either direction.
article.watch: A close above the 300.99 buy point, and the Oct. 29 earnings report that lands three sessions from now.

article.headline: Pfizer Wins FDA Nod For Talzenna-Xtandi Combo, Stock Dips 0.8%
article.deck: Pfizer is 1.6% past the 29.31 buy point of a six-week flat base, inside a buy range that runs to 30.78.
body: Pfizer fell 24 cents, or 0.8%, to 29.79 on Monday. The stock broke out Oct. 15 from a six-week flat base that ran 7.2% deep from its Sept. 3 high to its Oct. 5 low. The buy point is 29.31 and the buy range runs to 30.78; the close sits 1.6% past the buy point. Volume was 0.79 times the 50-day average, and the breakout session traded 0.97 times average.

The close is 2.1% below the 52-week high of 30.44. Pfizer is 5.1% above its 50-day line at 28.36 and 11.5% above its 200-day line at 26.71. It sits 1.15 ATRs from the 21-day line at 29.07, an intact trend. RS rank is 74 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 11.4% below its high. The stock is up 19.6% year to date and 18.0% over three months. The breakout is seven sessions old and still in range.

The June quarter showed a loss of 4 cents a share, down 107.8% from a year earlier, on revenue of $15.03 billion, up 2.6%. EPS ran 62 cents in the September 2025 quarter, a 29-cent loss in December and 47 cents in March. The forward P/E is 10.33. Pfizer reports next on Nov. 3.

The FDA approved Pfizer's Talzenna plus Xtandi for an earlier metastatic prostate cancer treatment setting, a headline said Monday. Sector headlines said healthcare stocks were softer in the afternoon.
A close under 29.31 would stall the breakout.
article.watch: Whether Pfizer holds the 21-day line at 29.07 into its Nov. 3 report.

article.headline: Visa Dips Before Tuesday Earnings; RBC Says Results May Top Views
article.deck: Visa is 4.8% past the 385.67 buy point of a six-week flat base and 79 cents from the 404.95 top of its buy range.
body: Visa fell 3.76, or 0.9%, to 404.16 on Monday. The stock broke out Oct. 12 from a six-week flat base that ran 7.5% deep from its Aug. 26 high to its Oct. 2 low. The buy point is 385.67 and the buy range runs to 404.95; the close sits 4.8% past the buy point, at the top edge of the range. Volume was 0.83 times the 50-day average, and the breakout session traded 0.80 times average.

The close is 2.5% below the 52-week high of 414.60. Visa is 7.0% above its 50-day line at 377.87 and 18.6% above its 200-day line at 340.82. It sits 1.61 ATRs from the 21-day line at 391.92, an intact trend. RS rank is 71 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 2.6% below its high. The stock is up 15.2% year to date. The breakout is 10 sessions old.

The June quarter showed earnings of $2.97 a share, up 10.4% from a year earlier, on revenue of $11.63 billion, up 14.4%. EPS ran $2.62, $3.03 and $3.14 in the three quarters before. The forward P/E is 26.90. Visa reports on Oct. 27.
RBC said Visa and Mastercard may top views as major fintech firms report this week. Another headline said Visa hit a record high despite a swipe-fee threat.
With the report due Tuesday and the stock at the top of its buy range, a close past 404.95 would leave it extended.
article.watch: The Oct. 27 earnings report and whether Visa holds the 21-day line at 391.92 after it.

market_note: The S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7676.77 and closed 0.3% below its 50-day line, the Nasdaq added 0.8% to 26169.38 and sits 1.6% under its 50-day, and the Dow gained 0.3% to 52361.58, 0.1% above its 50-day. The S&P 500 carries 5 distribution days over the last 25 sessions, the Nasdaq 3 and the Dow 4, and the desk's state remains Market in correction. After the close, Occidental Petroleum fell 7.0% to 59.60, GE Aerospace dropped 6.7% to 269.15 and Credo Technology rose 4.5% to 157.93. Leadership is thin but specific: Tesla, Berkshire Hathaway and monday.com are the three names in fresh breakouts this week, software leads the groups with an average RS rank of 73 and 88% of its names above the 50-day line, energy follows with 71% above it, and AI chips carry an average RS rank of 71 with only 17% of the group above the 50-day.

chief.verdict: The setups on the list are mostly defensive and slow: Berkshire, Visa, Exxon, Gilead and Pfizer sit in buy ranges while the Nasdaq trades 1.6% under its 50-day line and the ai infra group has only 6% of its names above the 50-day. The real growth leadership is thin and lives in software, where GitLab (RS rank 96) and Zeta (RS rank 94) hold tight in their buy ranges. Too many of the buyable names report inside the next four sessions (Visa on Oct. 27, Gilead and Cheniere on Oct. 29, Exxon on Oct. 30), and Nu's 17.0% drop on 4.36x average volume shows how fast a chart breaks in this tape, so the risk leans to the downside.
chief.market: With the desk's state at Market in correction and 5 distribution days on the S&P 500 (Nasdaq 3) over 25 sessions, exposure stays light: one or two small positions in the strongest charts, no full-size buys.
